newsitem.title: USA: Corporate bigwigs lobby for Hartford arena - paper.
newsitem.headline: Corporate bigwigs lobby for Hartford arena - paper.

text.p: An elite team of corporate heavyweights has quietly begun preparations for a statewide campaign to win corporate backing for a new sports arena, Hartford Courant reported Thursday.
The new Hartford arena would replace the Civic Center and provide a home for the National Hockey League's Hartford Whalers, according to the paper.
It would also be used by University of Connecticut sports teams and perhaps some national events such as the National Collegiate Athletic Association basketball championships.
The Whalers have threatened to leave Connecticut unless the state builds a new arena that could cost about $160 million.
Connecticut Gov. John Rowland is expected to announce soon whether the state can afford a new arena.

The Courant identified the corporate leaders who have begun laying groundwork for the new arena as Richard A. Higginbotham, Fleet Bank's president and chief executive for Connecticut; Robert W. Fiondella, chief executive at the Phoenix Home Life Mutual Insurance Co.; and Edward L. Morgan, Jr., a senior vice president at The Hartford and chairman of the Hartford Downtown Council.

A main thrust of their campaign is to persuade corporations in greater Hartford, greater New Haven and Fairfield County to promise to lease "luxury suites" -- bigger, more luxurious versions of the Civic Center's skyboxes -- in a new arena.
"In order to make the arena work, it's essential for the corporate community to get behind it," the paper quoted Greater Hartford Chamber of Commerce Chairman Thomas J. Groark, Jr., as saying.
